title: Turn DITL into executive-ready evidence
objective: Write a six-line DITL summary for the support case.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Executives don't need every click. They need the business consequence, the evidence behind it, and what is still uncertain.

items: **Business outcome:** what improves, and for whom.
**Current pain:** the friction and its cost of inaction.
**Future change:** what is different, and what stays the same.
**Value inputs:** population, frequency, and time or delay, each with units.
**Metric plan and open dependencies:** how it will be measured, and what must be resolved.

blocks.x: Link the detailed map so the SE, the value reviewer, and the customer owner can check it.

If two interviews report very different task times, investigate. Different personas, case types, or tools may explain the gap. Present a supported range or separate models per persona rather than a falsely precise average. Record who approved the interpretation.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: AI tools can draft DITL maps from transcripts, but any step duration they produce is unverified until the customer confirms it. Mark generated timings as unverified, and get customer evidence before modeling.
Six lines carry a DITL into the executive readout. Each line should be traceable to an interview or a metric card.

blocks.title: The six-line DITL summary
blocks.alt: Six stacked lines of a DITL summary: the business outcome, the current pain, the future change, the value inputs, the evidence strength, and the metric plan with open dependencies.
